query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The incorporation of 5 vol% low-melting In particles and 2 vol% carbon nanotubes into the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy via spark plasma sintering will improve the compressive strength and thermal conductivity of the alloy, while maintaining its large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation.
generation.intervention: Incorporation of 5 vol% low-melting In particles and 2 vol% carbon nanotubes into the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy via spark plasma sintering
generation.conditions: Applied-field: 5 T, pressure-field: 100 MPa, temperature range: 250-350 K, loading regime: cyclic compressive loading
generation.mechanism: The In particles will enhance thermal conductivity and provide a ductile phase to improve toughness, while the carbon nanotubes will increase the compressive strength and provide a percolating network for heat transport, thus overcoming the cracking issue and maintaining the caloric response
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved compressive strength (>200 MPa), enhanced thermal conductivity (>8 times that of epoxy-containing samples), and maintained large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation
generation.boundary: The alloy will be tested under applied-field and pressure-field operation, with a temperature range of 250-350 K and a loading regime of cyclic compressive loading
generation.uncertainty: The main risk associated with this direction is that the addition of In particles and carbon nanotubes may not be sufficient to completely overcome the cracking issue, or may affect the caloric response negatively

falsification_experiment.design: A controlled experiment will be designed to test the hypothesis, where the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy with and without the addition of In particles and carbon nanotubes will be subjected to applied-field and pressure-field operation, and their compressive strength, thermal conductivity, and caloric response will be measured
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of In particles and carbon nanotubes does not result in an improvement in compressive strength and thermal conductivity, or if the caloric response is negatively affected, the hypothesis will be falsified
